compute.reported_as: TABLE II: Energy per site in some open-shell Hubbard square lattices at U = 4. The symmetry of the ground state, S^2 = 0, Kx = Ky = 0, is preserved in the trial wave function used in CP/SYM and RC/SYM. The UHF trial wave function is generated with U = 0.5 as has been done before. (...) The RC results in Table II are essentially exact ground-state energies. || From a converged CP calculation, one can release the constraint (...) CP calculations will scale as a low power of the system size; FP and RC will of course have exponential scaling from the sign problem, albeit at a much reduced level with the proposed symmetry improvements. || Cost statements exist only for other calculations in the paper: Fig. 2 (FP, 8x8, N_up = N_dn = 32, U = 8, Hartree-Fock trial wave function): "The number of walkers was 10^5, with a total 20 separate runs to obtain the final averages and estimate the error bars."; Fig. 3 (FP, 4x4, N_up = N_dn = 7, U = 8): "The number of walkers is 5 x 10^5, with total 100 separate runs to estimate the error bars."; Fig. 4 (FP, periodic 8x8, N_up = N_dn = 13, U = 4): "The run took ~ 17 hours on 100 AMD Opteron 2.4GHz cores."; Fig. 5 (RC, 4x4, N_up = N_dn = 7, U = 8): "The number of walkers is 1 x 10^5, with total 100 runs in the RC portion to collect statistics."; Sec. III C example: "CPMC has 10,000 walkers, with back-propagation beta = 1." || We also acknowledge a DOE CMCSN award for facilitating stimulating interactions, and an INCITE award for computing using resources of the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

compute.reported_as: Our implementation utilizes Jax [29] to perform automatic differentiation and sampling, alongside the Optax package [30] for optimization. (...) Optimization generally uses around 180 optimization steps with varying and decaying step size (see appendix); gradients are accumulated with 189,000 samples and parameters are updated using a random step with the computed sign [11]. || After optimization, parameters are selected based on the lowest observed average energy. Using this parameter set, observables such as the local energy and electron occupation are measured with approximately 10^6 samples with a thermalization of 10^3 sweeps. || Most of these parameters are in T_l^sigma, with O(N_l * N^2) parameters. || The step sizes during the first 79 steps of optimization is 0.01 and then is lowered to 0.001 for the remaining 100 steps. The optimal point is selected by the lowest energy during the optimization, normally somewhere after the first 80 steps. Optimization was performed with 126 independent walkers contributing to the total sample collection, while the additional measurement of the optimized parameters used 120 walkers. Each measurement was collected after N * N_l Metropolis updates and values reported in the main text were averaged over walkers and a 1000 sweep thermalization time was used. (...) Variance measurement was performed with an additional 10x samples.
compute.source: Sec. II A Implementation Details; Sec. II (parameter scaling); Appendix A Further Computational Details, arXiv:2308.08594 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Blanket statements for all VAFQMC (N_l = 4) results; nothing is given per system size. samples = the "approximately 10^6 samples" used for the final energy measurement; gradients during optimization used 189,000 samples per step; 126 walkers (optimization) / 120 walkers (measurement); 1000-sweep thermalization; variance measured with 10x more samples. iterations = "around 180 optimization steps" (79 at step size 0.01 + 100 at 0.001 per Appendix A). Parameter count not stated, only the scaling O(N_l * N^2), dominated by the T_l^sigma hopping matrices. No hardware, GPU/CPU-hours or wall-clock stated anywhere (JAX + Optax implementation; affiliation Flatiron Institute, no machine named).
